lesson.menu_desc: The Vancouver story + past continuous vs past simple -- 30 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 11 -- Telling a Travel Story
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Thiago Negrães | Lesson 11 -- Telling a Travel Story

listenings.text: Hi, I am Rachel, and this is my worst travel day. I was flying from Seattle to Vancouver for a conference. While I was waiting at the gate, they announced that the flight was canceled. Everybody ran to the desk. I was standing in the line when the man behind me offered to share a rental car. It sounds crazy, but I said yes. We were driving north along the coast when the sun came up, and it turned out to be the most beautiful morning of my life. I missed the first day of the conference, but I have never regretted it.

Hi Thiago, it is Mark, your host dad. I just want to tell you what happened this afternoon, because you were at school. I was cooking dinner when the power went out in the whole street. While I was looking for candles, the neighbors knocked on the door and invited us to a cookout in their backyard. So we ended up eating there, and it was a lot of fun. When you get home, do not go to our house, it is completely dark. Come next door, to the blue house. There is a plate of food waiting for you.

extra_audio.text: First, Thiago was living in a homestay and studying at a language school. Then, on his first Saturday, he went sightseeing and got lost. After that, he was walking along the water when, all of a sudden, it started to rain. Next, while he was looking for a bus stop, he ran into a classmate. Finally, they ended up in a small restaurant, and it turned out to be the best night of the trip.

items.situation: A colleague asks what you were doing in Vancouver for a month.
tips: The whole month is the background: was plus -ing.
Say where you were living, too.

items.situation: You want to say what the weather did while you were walking along the water.
tips: The walk was in progress, the rain started at one moment.
Use when, and one of the new expressions for a surprise.

items.situation: Tell somebody you met a classmate by chance at a bus stop.
tips: There is a two-word verb for meeting by chance.
Start with while for the long action.

items.situation: You planned to go home, but you spent three hours in a restaurant.
tips: There is a two-word verb for a place you did not plan.
Past simple: the first verb takes -ed.

items.situation: A bad start became the best night of the trip. Say it.
tips: There is a two-word verb for a result you did not expect.
It ... to be the best night.
